expert_role: Environmental psychology researcher on spatial experience, acting as gatekeeper source auditor (round 3, packet P12)

findings.issue: The vestibule rule is misstated. The spec models 'two door lines at least 2.1 m apart' with area 'at most 4.65 m2 or 2%'. VBBL 2019 10.2.2.8(1)(c), which I read in the same consolidation the spec cites, requires at least 4.87 m between doors where the level's gross conditioned floor area is 3,716.1 m2 or more and the doors have automatic, electrically driven closers. A full-block podium on an 11,468 m2 site with automatic lobby doors almost certainly falls in this case. At 4.87 m the 4.65 m2 cap cannot be met, so the 2% branch governs. The exemption list is also incomplete in the spec: entrances with revolving doors, doors not used as entrances, buildings under 278.7 m2, and enclosed elevator lobbies entered from parking garages. Whether the below-grade transit-link entrance counts as an exterior entrance is not addressed. In winter, stack effect in a 300 m tower drives the strongest inflow through exactly these low entrances.
findings.fix: Encode 10.2.2.8(1)(b) and (c) as a rule that picks door separation (2.1 m or 4.87 m) from level area and door type, and switches the area cap to the 2% branch. Add the full exemption list. Feed vestibule depth into M01's entry sequence. Flag the transit-link entrance's exterior or interior status as UNRESOLVED, with a stack-effect note linked to M08 and SYST. Keep the rule as legacy_version until VBBL 2025 is read.

findings.issue: The egress basis still treats the occupant-load table as unread ('office factor 9.3 m2/person is recalled, unverified') and cites the Part 9 sleeping-area rule. The open BC Publications VBBL 2019 Division B Section 3.1 (consolidated to 1 Jul 2024) gives Table 3.1.17.1 values: offices 9.30, dining/beverage 1.20, non-fixed seats 0.75, standing space 0.40, mercantile basements and first storeys 3.70, mercantile other storeys 5.60, kitchens 9.30 m2/person. Its Part 3 wording is '2 persons per sleeping room in a dwelling unit', not 'bedroom or sleeping area'. Hotel guest rooms are not dwelling units, so the spec's '2 persons per sleeping area' for hotels has no clause behind it.
findings.fix: Load Table 3.1.17.1 as legacy_version, citing the Section 3.1 URL as a new source, with each value tagged to its area basis. Replace the Part 9 citation (P12-S51) with Article 3.1.17.1(1)(b). Set the hotel egress basis to the 'designed number, not less than table' clause and mark it UNRESOLVED until a professional or VBBL 2025 confirms it. Close the UNVERIFIED flag for the 2019 edition.

findings.issue: After three rounds the VTC brief PDF is still unopened (P12-S48 opened=false, although its extract says 'summary page opened earlier'). The 9.0 FSR test in the core module, the site size, the transit link and all four jury weights that drive the jury_criteria tags come from the team's own summary. The competition page timed out for me as well. An entrant cannot rely on a core pass/fail-style FSR bar whose definition has never been read.
findings.fix: Open the brief PDF before 13 Nov. Record page and clause for site dimensions, the FSR wording and floor-area definition, the height range, the transit link and the jury weights. Make the opened flag consistent with the extract. Until then, show the FSR bar as 'brief unread'.

findings.issue: The headline metric 'mean visual integration' and method step 4 attribute integration to Turner et al. (2001). The paper's text, which I decoded, never uses the word 'integration'. It reports neighbourhood size, clustering coefficient and mean shortest path length, and gives grid guidance (a 'human-scale' spacing of about 1 m). The normalisation in 'Normalised mean shortest-path length per connected visibility graph' is undefined, so two implementations, or the browser result and depthmapXcli, can disagree with no way to say which is right. The course rule 'show its work' is not met.
findings.fix: State the exact formula, for example Hillier and Hanson relative asymmetry with D-value normalisation as implemented in depthmapX, and cite its true source (Hillier and Hanson 1984 or the depthmapX source code) as a new record. Otherwise report MSPL ranks only and rename the metric. Add an acceptance test: on one reference plan, the browser field must match depthmapXcli within a stated tolerance.

findings.issue: The criterion worth 40% of the jury score has no metric grounded in how people perceive or use interior space. The packet measures codes, credits and graph geometry but not experience. Evidence exists and was not used. Wiener et al. (2007, Perception 36:1066-1083) found strong correlations between isovist measures and both affective appraisal and navigation across 16 virtual indoor scenes. Franz and Wiener (2008, EPB 35:574-592) map isovist measures to perceived spaciousness and openness. Hölscher et al. (2006, JEP 26:284-299) study wayfinding across floors, which is the core problem at sky-lobby transfers. LEED v5 EQc2 itself offers Option 1 Path 1 (biophilic principles after Kellert and Calabrese) and Option 2 (prospect-and-refuge seating, an accessible quiet space). Prospect-refuge appears in M01 only as free text.
findings.fix: Add perception metrics to M01 or a new SPAC module. (a) Isovist experiential descriptors (area, compactness, jaggedness or occlusivity) labelled 'lab VR evidence, relative only'. (b) Peak crowding density in lift lobbies and sky lobbies, from M04 PeakCoincident divided by lobby area, with no threshold until a source is opened. (c) A vertical-wayfinding check: floor-change points, and whether lifts are visible from the sky-lobby arrival point. (d) A refuge-availability count (seating with back cover and an outlook). (e) Ceiling height or volume per person in public rooms. All are team_assumption reference values, and their meaning is a human judgement record.

findings.issue: The core cut grew from 12-15 to 15-18 person-days (M04 6-8, M06a 3, M06b 4, X01 2-3). From Wed 21 Oct to Fri 13 Nov there are 17 working days, less Remembrance Day (11 Nov), which is about 34 person-days for two students across every packet. P12 core alone takes 44-53% of total capacity. The notes call capacity a team assumption but do not resolve it.
findings.fix: Re-cut the core to M04 (egress and FSR only), M06a WWR and openings, the M06b bird-zone share plus VLT, and a minimal X01 (evidence_status to badge). Move SHGC lines, U waterfall and vestibule counts to v1. State the remaining P12 share of capacity in the notes.

findings.issue: Eye height: the spec says 1.2 m is 'the grid height REHVA gives for EN 17037 view out'. In REHVA, the seated 1.2 m grid belongs to the authors' own computational method. REHVA does not quote it as a clause of EN 17037.
findings.fix: Label 1.2 m as 'authors' method (REHVA 04/2023); EN 17037 Annex C text unopened' and keep both eye heights as presets.

findings.issue: LEEDuser lists EQc2 as 1-7 points in total, but the spec presents views (up to 3), proximity (1) and sDA (up to 4) as independent tallies. The spec also omits Option 5 Path 1, solar glare control (1 pt), and Options 3 (ASHRAE 55-2023) and 4 (sound mapping and criteria), which bear on M03 glare and on M08.
findings.fix: Show the 7-point cap in any LEED roll-up. Add the solar-glare-control path as a checklist item in M03. In M08, cite the v5 thermal and sound options as secondary references (still no numbers).

findings.issue: UBC limits fly-through elimination to 'up to 16 m or 4 m above tallest vegetation'. The spec's metric (0 fly-throughs anywhere) is stricter than the source but is not labelled as such. The same Backgrounder warns against untreated glass within 2-20 m of vegetation (Cusa et al. 2015) and against indoor plants visible through glass. Atria, winter gardens and sky gardens in this packet create both conditions.
findings.fix: Label the whole-height fly-through rule as a team rule that goes beyond UBC. Add a flag for glazing within 20 m of planted terraces and for interior planting visible through glass (secondary, UBC citing Cusa 2015).

findings.issue: The packet's only metric marked 'verified' (M07 GWP per material) rests on the CLF BC guide. The guide compiles EC3 values and carries an all-rights-reserved notice, so it is not the primary EPD. X01 Rule 1 (primary source, opened, in force) should therefore downgrade it, and X01 as specified would flag its own packet.
findings.fix: Cite the underlying EPDs (Butler 28 d, Cascade) as primary records, or set evidence_status to verified_secondary. Note that Burnco 166 is a 56-day value.

findings.issue: Seven metrics carry 'false_assumption_corrected' as their evidence_status, and some also use it as status. This replaces the evidence tier of the corrected value: the M06b TEUI line is in fact legacy_version, and the M03 sDA and proximity metrics are verified_secondary. The X01 rule that 'legacy_version blocks badges' never sees them, and the four-value status enum does not include this value.
findings.fix: Add a separate boolean or history field 'corrected_in_round'. Set evidence_status to the tier of the new source and keep status within its four-value enum.

findings.issue: M07's FacadeCarbonTable and its WWR curve are drawn 'beside the TEDI result from ENER'. ENER runs after M06b, which reads M07 assemblies, so if M07 renders ENER output the graph has a cycle M07 -> M06b -> ENER -> M07. The TEDI sweep over WWR would also need repeated ENER runs, and none are specified.
findings.fix: Move the paired chart to a display node downstream of both ENER and M07. Specify the TEDI sweep as an ENER batch job, or show TEDI only at the current WWR.

findings.issue: Curtain-wall vision glass is always processed (low-e coated, heat-strengthened or laminated) and assembled into IGUs. The CLF 2023 table gives 1,430 kgCO2e/t only for unprocessed annealed flat glass and 'none' for processed glass and IGUs. The method 'm2 x thickness x density x GWP per tonne' therefore always gives a lower bound for this building type.
findings.fix: Label every glass result calculated from the flat-glass baseline as a 'lower bound (annealed)', and require a product IGU EPD before facade systems are compared.

findings.issue: The energy-path summary leaves out two alternatives in 10.2.2.5: GHGI compliance is waived if Table 10.2.2.5.B TEUI and TEDI are met (sentence 3), and certified Passive House designs are deemed to comply (sentence 4). Both change which limit line an entrant should read.
findings.fix: List the A1, B and C tables and the Passive House route as alternative legacy_version reference lines, with a selector.

verdict: Round 3 is honest and well caveated, and most round-2 items are fixed. The VBBL energy, UBC, LEED v5, CLF and Turner figures check out against the sources. The gate fails on five points. First, the vestibule rule leaves out the 4.87 m clause that probably governs a full-block podium. Second, the VBBL 2019 Part 3 occupant-load table is readable but still marked unverified. Third, the VTC brief behind the core FSR test is still unopened. Fourth, the headline M01 'integration' metric is attributed to a paper that never defines it. Fifth, the 40% human-scale criterion has no metric grounded in perception, although relevant isovist and wayfinding studies exist. The core scope also exceeds realistic capacity. All six conditions can be fixed within days.
